Author: Abigail Rueger, MA Medical Reviewer: Kristen Fuller, MD

ChoosingTherapy.com may earn commissions from the companies reviewed when you click links on this page. Learn more about our editorial standards, review process, and advertising policy.

SonderMind is a platform offering online therapy and psychiatry nationwide. Its main focus is on providing mental healthcare to people who want to use their insurance plans, as it helps therapists get credentialed with more providers so they can offer care without worrying about billing. SonderMind’s network includes more than 12,000 mental healthcare providers, and its app is convenient for users looking to find a therapist or psychiatrist who takes their insurance. SonderMind at a Glance Rating: (4 out of 5) Cost: Varies by provider & insurance plan

Insurance accepted: Yes

Medication available: Yes Get Started Visit SonderMind Pros & Cons Pros Pros In-network with most major insurance plans

Offers both therapy and medication

Convenient app with extra mindfulness features

Message your providers through the app any time Cons Cons Cash pay prices are not listed on therapist’s profiles

Customer service is slow Preview SonderMind SonderMind makes it easy to find a therapist or medication prescriber who is in-network with your insurance plan. Sign up by responding to a few prompts about what type of provider you’re looking for, your name and contact information, and your insurance provider if you plan on using it. You can do this on your web browser on your computer or phone, or by using SonderMind’s app, which I found to be quite user-friendly. When I found a therapist through SonderMind, I was able to sign up within about 10 minutes and I saw my therapist five days later. I like that everything was easy to navigate or change within the app, and that the app had a few extra features, like guided meditations and goal-setting with the help of an AI chatbot. SonderMind could be a great choice for many people looking for online mental healthcare, especially for those looking to use their insurance for either therapy or medication (or both). If SonderMind isn’t in-network with your insurance plan, we recommend checking out Brightside Health or Grow Therapy for both therapy and psychiatry. Brightside uses a monthly subscription format, while Grow acts more as a directory where you can choose your own provider(s). Detailed Review of SonderMind SonderMind is a full-service mental health app, offering insurance-based therapy, psychiatry, and extra features like meditations and an AI chatbot to help with goal setting and tracking. I found that SonderMind made it incredibly easy to sign up and get started seeing a therapist right away. SonderMind earned 4 out of 5 stars View Details Detailed Scoring Breakdown Clientele Served (5 out of 5) Range of Therapist Specialties & Treatment Approaches (5 out of 5) Geographic Location (4.5 out of 5) Session Length & Provider Consistency (5 out of 5) Ongoing Access to Your Provider (5 out of 5) Online Therapy Cost (2 out of 5) Payment Options, Insurance, & Out-of-Network Benefits (3 out of 5) Therapist Matching or Selection (3.5 out of 5) Client Interface & User Experience (5 out of 5) Privacy & HIPAA (5 out of 5) Therapist Credentials & Expertise (5 out of 5) Customer Service (2 out of 5) Reliability & Longevity (5 out of 5) Review our scoring criteria for online therapy platforms here.

Review our complete editorial policies here. Therapist Matching SonderMind’s directory is automatically personalized with results that fit your state and insurance plan after you fill out some basic information and create an account. I didn’t love that I couldn’t see my therapist options before giving SonderMind my phone number and email address and setting up an account—what if I didn’t find someone in my state who took my insurance who felt like a good fit? You must also add your insurance and payment information before you’re allowed to schedule an appointment, though this seems reasonable to me. When I signed up, I included in the “additional preferences” text box that I would prefer a queer therapist, and I appreciated that the top populated options were self-identified queer therapists. However, I was a bit surprised to see that there were only eight therapists listed as potential options for me. This may be because I selected cash-pay and it focuses on insurance credentialing, but there was no way for me to go back and see what my options were if I selected an insurance plan. I selected my top option (who truly did seem like the best choice out of the therapists listed, so points there!), then booked an appointment directly from her profile. Within an hour or so, she had messaged me saying she wasn’t available at the time I booked but gave me a few other options, and in the end I had a therapy appointment scheduled for five days after I reached out. Online Therapy Sessions My online session with SonderMind went smoothly, and joining was as simple as clicking a button on the client dashboard. My therapist was about three minutes late, but once on we had no issues with either sound or video quality through its platform. I felt the therapist was a great match for my needs, as she was able to talk to me about her professional experience helping clients with issues similar to mine. She asked several great questions about my preferences for therapy, like whether I wanted her to self-disclose, what types of therapy I’ve tried (and what I liked and didn’t like about each), and what I felt like wasn’t helpful from my previous therapy experiences so she could calibrate around what I was looking for. She was responsive and also a good listener, and was totally open to my preferences as far as how often we meet, what we want to focus on together, and whether or not I wanted homework for the goals we talked about working toward together. At the 50-minute mark, we were naturally at a good stopping point (she timed the session quite well), and we then each looked at our schedules to book a next session. Immediately after our session, I got an email from SonderMind with a three-question quiz to fill out asking about the therapeutic alliance between my therapist and me. The three points were, “In the session, we discussed the things most important to me,” “I feel understood and respected by my provider,” and “I understand and agree with my treatment plan.” I felt a little overwhelmed getting an email asking me to fill out more forms right after having an intake session, but those three questions all felt like really good baselines for determining therapist fit, so I didn’t mind. Medication Management SonderMind’s medication services work largely similarly to its therapy platform, and it has providers available nationwide through insurance and cash-pay. When I selected that I was interested in psychiatry in the SonderMind app just to see how it worked and navigate around the platform, I was notified that two different prescribers would reach out to me within the next 2–3 business days, or I could choose from three more options if I preferred. I had a call come in from a prescriber the next day (which I ignored, oops!), and when I didn’t return the call, I was automatically scheduled for an appointment with that provider for a week later. I cancelled that appointment as I don’t need medication management at this time, but I thought it was interesting that it was automatically scheduled. Since you may have to pay if you don’t cancel within 24 hours, you may want to make sure you pay attention to any notifications you get and be aware of any sessions that may get scheduled on your behalf. It is unclear whether SonderMind providers can prescribe controlled substances (like Adderall for ADHD or benzodiazepines like Xanax and Klonopin for certain kinds of anxiety), so be sure to ask your provider directly if you suspect you may need these types of medication. Additional Features The SonderMind app also offers a few extra features, including a goal-setting tab with an AI chatbot to help you determine some goals, as well as use the tool as a journaling space to track your moods and see what progress you’ve made toward your goals. There are also a couple of mindfulness tools, including guided meditations and breathing exercises and calming sounds with titles like “Serene Dream,” “Carefree,” and “Let It Glide.” SonderMind also just launched a few more AI features to help with therapy session notes and goals. These include a note-taking feature for therapists, plus session prep and session Takeaways for clients to be able to focus their goals for sessions beforehand and know what to work on between appointments. SonderMind Cost & Insurance It’s incredibly difficult to determine what cash-pay prices will be when you sign up for therapy on SonderMind, as I didn’t see these rates listed on the therapist profiles I looked through. If you’re planning on paying with cash, you should message your provider to determine this cost. Candid Health plans to dig deeper into “the largest and most complex healthcare organizations in the country,” said Proctor, “meeting the industry where it’s hardest to operate and proving what modern RCM can do at enterprise scale.” Purpose-built AI and machine learning, embedded natively into the Candid platform, is central to this new chapter.

With expanded AI/ML capabilities, customers can expect fully automated workflows, predictive claim submission, and configurable tools that give administrative staff even more time to focus on high-value patient interactions.

Talkiatry Attributes its Growth During the Past Year to the Expansion of its National Clinical Workforce and its Dedication to Scaling Accessible, In-Network Behavioral Health Care NEW YORK, Nov. 19, 2025 /PRNewswire/ -- Talkiatry today announced it ranked 56 on the Deloitte Technology Fast 500 ™, a ranking of the 500 fastest-growing technology, media, telecommunications, life sciences, fintech, and energy tech companies in North America, now in its 31st year. Talkiatry's continued growth is powered by the expansion of its fulltime clinical workforce and its investments in evidence-based care delivery, advanced clinical infrastructure, and specialized treatment programs that reach previously underserved populations, including children, seniors, and new mothers. This award reflects the company's commitment to building a more reliable, integrated, and accessible behavioral health system nationwide. "We're honored to be recognized on Deloitte's Technology Fast 500 for the second consecutive year. This achievement reflects our commitment to providing exceptional clinical care, led by our team of more than 800 psychiatrists and 300 therapists," said Robert Krayn, CEO and cofounder of Talkiatry. "Together, we're pushing behavioral health care forward and ensuring patients across the country can access mental health care that is consistent and rooted in clinical excellence. As Talkiatry looks to the future of behavioral health, we remain focused on raising the standard for behavioral health care and expanding what's possible for both patients and providers." "This year's rankings highlight both enduring leadership and breakthrough momentum," said Wolfe Tone, US Deloitte Private & Emerging Client Portfolio leader and partner, Deloitte Tax LLP. "More than half of the winners are prior honorees, yet the majority of the top ten are first-time entrants — demonstrating the staying power of established leaders alongside the accelerating growth of new innovators across key sectors. As in previous years, private companies continue to dominate, underscoring the agility that private enterprises bring to competitive markets, enabling the exceptional triple and quadruple digit growth reflected in these rankings." Talkiatry was also a Technology Fast 500 award winner for 2024. Overall, 2025 Technology Fast 500 companies achieved revenue growth ranging from 122% to 29,738% over the three-year time frame, with an average growth rate of 1,079%. About Talkiatry

Talkiatry is a national mental health practice that provides in-network psychiatry and therapy. They were co-founded by a patient and a triple-board-certified psychiatrist to solve the problems both groups face in accessing and providing the highest quality mental healthcare. 60% of adults in the U.S. with a diagnosable mental illness go untreated every year because care is inaccessible, while 45% of clinicians are out of network with insurers because reimbursement rates are low and paperwork is unduly burdensome. With innovative technology and a human-centered philosophy, Talkiatry provides patients with the care they need—and allows psychiatrists to focus on why they got into medicine. Learn more at www.talkiatry.com and follow us on Instagram , TikTok , and LinkedIn . About the 2025 Deloitte Technology Fast 500

Now in its 31st year, the Deloitte Technology Fast 500 provides a ranking of the fastest-growing technology, media, telecommunications, life sciences, fintech, and energy tech companies — both public and private — in North America. Technology Fast 500 award winners are selected based on percentage fiscal year revenue growth from 2021 to 2024. In order to be eligible for Technology Fast 500 recognition, companies must own proprietary intellectual property or proprietary technology that significantly contributes to the company's operating revenues. Companies must have base-year operating revenues of at least US$50,000, and current-year operating revenues of at least US$5 million, with a growth rate of 50% or greater. Additionally, companies must be in business for a minimum of four years and be headquartered within North America (United States and Canada). *Please see www.deloitte.com/us/about for a detailed description of their legal structure.
